purpose: Seed inventory of public AI incident, failure, and threat sources for metadata-only availability monitoring. This is not an exhaustive global census.

sources.title: AI Incident Database (AIID)
sources.coverage_note: Indexes reported real-world AI harms and near-harms; source and language coverage follow its curation and reporting inputs.
sources.reuse_note: The terms license specified snapshot collections under CC BY-SA. Submissions, the report text field, and linked media/content are excluded. The snapshots page asks users to contact the project about their use case.

sources.title: AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor
sources.coverage_note: Daily event pipeline based on news intelligence, AI-assisted classification and clustering; not a complete record of private or under-reported events.
sources.reuse_note: Public monitor and methodology are documented. Bulk data reuse terms are not recorded here; do not copy records until the applicable terms are confirmed.

sources.title: AI, Algorithmic and Automation Incidents and Controversies Repository
sources.coverage_note: Manually compiled public-interest repository; its definitions and qualitative inclusion criteria differ from other sources.
sources.reuse_note: The user guide says use should be substantially in the public interest, adapted or redistributed material should remain CC BY-SA 4.0, and commercial risk-management or text-analysis products/services are outside its stated permitted use.

sources.title: AVID database
sources.coverage_note: Structured reports and vulnerability records for general-purpose AI failures; not a general social-harm incident census.
sources.reuse_note: The database is described as open source, but the applicable data-record license and reuse terms are not recorded in this registry.

sources.title: ATLAS threat knowledge base
sources.coverage_note: Threat tactics, techniques, mitigations and case studies for attacks involving AI; this is contextual threat intelligence, not a general incident-report database.
sources.reuse_note: Track as a separate security context source. Review release and licensing terms before copying case-study content.

sources.title: AI Incident Index data releases
sources.coverage_note: A newer cross-source index. Treat its own records and its linked third-party source material as separate evidence layers.
sources.reuse_note: Its terms state that the Index dataset is CC BY 4.0; cited third-party material remains under its own owners' terms. Validate release provenance, deduplication and scope before use.

sources.title: AI Act Article 73 serious-incident reporting
sources.coverage_note: An official reporting obligation and authority workflow, not an open incident-record corpus.
sources.reuse_note: No reporting submissions are accessed or collected by this monitor.
